title.narrative: TZA - Bilaterale landenportefeuille Tanzania 2023-2028 - Interventie WASKIRP
TZA - Programme de cooperation Tanzania 2023-2028 - Intervention WASKIRP

description.narrative: In the WASKIRP project, several delays in the infrastructure development have led that none of the water schemes have been completed and handed over to Community-Based Water Supply Organizations (CBWSOs) while the establishment and registration of CBWOs has been completed. Thus, despite being established and trained in some respects, none of the 6 CBWSOs has started actively to play their roles in the water schemes management. Nevertheless, as capacity building of the CBWSOs is essential to ensure the sustainability of the water schemes (built under the WASKIRP project), a sustainable skill base needs to be achieved through regular updating of knowledge. The actions below aim to strengthen skills and capacity of the CBWSOs to ensure the sustainability management of the water schemes to the ultimate benefit of population. Currently, CBWOs have weaknesses in their capacity to manage facilities. Their lack of skills and insufficient technical capacity limit proper management of water schemes. They need support in the areas of governance, human resources, data management, sustainable financing, development and implementation of effective operations and management plans, and water protection among others. The CBWSOs are under overall coordination of RUWASA which supports CBWSOs in relation to management, operation and maintenance of rural water supply schemes; facilitate their training and capacity building; their register and regulates their performances. RUWASA (Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency) is integrated into the process to develop its own capacity to supervise the CBWSOs and monitor the infrastructure until final acceptance is granted. The general objective as defined in the WASKIRP specific agreement reads: “Equitable development and poverty reduction among Kigoma communities are improved through access to safe and clean water supply and sanitation services (WASKIRP)”. The specific objective to which replies this punctual intervention reads “Community in Kigoma Region especially women and youth have an increased access to safe drinking water and burden related to water and sanitation is reduced”. The activities proposed under this phasing-out complement and anchor 1 result considered in the specific agreement: A1. Community Owned Water Supply Organisations are managing rural water supply schemes in a sustainable way. The project is rehabilitating existing water supply assets and constructing new ones while preparing the capacity of local communities and the Rural Water Supply Agency (RUWASA) to manage the infrastructure funded by the project. The project is being implemented in 6 Districts of Kigoma Region and is expected to serve a total population of about 200,000 people by the end of 2023 The WaSKiRP_PhaseOut (Water and Sanitation Kigoma Region Project) project aims to contribute towards equitable development and poverty reduction among Kigoma rural communities through improved access to safe and clean water supply and sanitation services. Its specific objective is to increase access to safe/clean water and sanitation services and reduce burden related to water & sanitation among communities in Kigoma region, especially women and youths, and use the water as social economic commodity through sustainable interventions on water supply and hygiene practices.
